column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 to ISO/IEC 29100:2011 Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the ISO/IEC 22989:2022 (Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology) and ISO/IEC 29100:2011 (Privacy framework) LinkML schemas. Mappings link AI-side stakeholders and personal-data references to the ISO/IEC 29100 PII flow roles and information categories, plus the trustworthiness privacy property to the privacy-framework root.

column10: Shared identity / labelled-entity abstraction at the root of both schemas.
ISO/IEC 22989 data subject (an AI subject whose personal data is processed) corresponds to the ISO/IEC 29100 PII principal.
A data provider supplying personal data acts as a PII controller when determining purposes and means of processing.
AI producers processing personal data on behalf of a controller act as PII processors.
AI partners other than the controller, processor or principal correspond to ISO/IEC 29100 third parties.
A dataset containing personal data is composed of PII as defined in ISO/IEC 29100.
The PII abbreviation in ISO/IEC 22989 references the same concept as ISO/IEC 29100 PII.
Data processes acting on personal data realise PII processing activities.
De-identification of PII is an ISO/IEC 29100 PII-processing operation.
Privacy as a trustworthiness property is operationalised through an ISO/IEC 29100-aligned privacy framework.
The privacy trustworthiness property aggregates the ISO/IEC 29100 privacy principles.
Privacy risks affecting an AI system are a specialisation of AI risk items.
